Also, she requires we pay taxes for the gear too in case we work together: "I’m really sorry to bring this up, but German tax bureaucracy loves to make things a bit complicated... Since this is a barter deal, receiving gear worth over €10,000 counts as a non-cash benefit (geldwerter Vorteil). If I keep the gear, the German tax office treats it like regular income, meaning I’d have to pay heavy taxes on it out of my own pocket just to accept the package—which would sadly take away a bit of the joy of this collaboration. The good news: German tax law (§ 37b EStG) actually has a very elegant solution for this. Companies can opt to pay a flat-rate tax of 30% (plus solidary surcharge) on behalf of the creator. This covers the tax burden completely, and both sides are 100% safe and compliant. Would Hasselblad be able to take over this flat-rate tax for the gear? Let me know what you think, and I'll keep you posted on my timeline!" 5/7 hongtao老师通知移交scofield
